svg.title: RIEMANN T1 — The deepest chain: from a count of lattices by isometries up to the Riemann Hypothesis
svg.desc: One chain through the proof: 11 statements, each used by the proof of the next, from lem-local-lattice-counts-isometries at depth 10 up to thm-riemann-hypothesis of Main.lean. It is a shortest chain in the blueprint's uses graph, found breadth-first from the three theorems nothing else uses, so every statement on it is as far from the main theorems as it can be. Read it as a proof, left to right and top to bottom: nothing is used before it is proved. Each card is one blueprint statement, as in the chapter posters; an arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A. This is how deep the proof goes: no statement of the blueprint is farther from the main theorems than the first card. The chain runs through the families, the off-diagonal bound of the theta chapter, and down to a local lattice count. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

marks the theorem the chain ends in.

The Lean panel is the signature of the first declaration the blueprint lists for the statement, as lean-facts.json records it, wrapped and cut at nine lines. The footer gives its file and line in the mirror and
the other declarations.
The line in italics is the blueprint's statement, and the bullets are its proof, paragraph by paragraph, abridged where marked with …; links appear as ids and maths is rewritten in plain Unicode.
Proof uses and Used by list every edge, not only the one the chain takes: the chain is one path through a tree, and the footers show where the other branches go.

theorem integralClosureRank_and_residueTrdegLe (D :
Formalism.BasicNotions.D7) :
Formalism.MainNotions.ThinScalesBound.T2 D
Let F be a non-archimedean local field, E/F the local algebra of the datum D with a good model,
and V a hermitian E-space of the dimension of D. Let t_1 be generic data for a flag of length
r+1, and f_2, f_2' frames with isometries φ, φ' to the spans of t_1, fixing the last vectors.
Let P_1, P_2 be the Gram matrices of t_1 and of (f_2, f_2'), and S the set of generic
lattices compatible with these data. If a determinant Δ attached to t_1 is 0, then |S| is the
number of isometries between P_1 and P_2.
The cases Δ = 0 and Δ a unit are proved separately and combined.
Stated with no other statement
Proof uses nothing the blueprint names

theorem partnerCount_holds_all {D : Formalism.BasicNotions.D7} (Zd
: Formalism.L2.SG.TermLoc.LocDat D) : PartnerIsomorphismCount
Zd
Let D be a datum with local models M_p, and p a finite place. Take generic local data t_1 for a
flag of length r+1, frames f_2, f_2' and isometries φ, φ' between the spans, meeting the
local counting hypotheses. Suppose the Gram matrices of t_1 and of (f_2, f_2') have LU
-decompositions u_L Z u_U, with unipotent u_L, u_U, through the same model matrix up to
the kind of the point. Then the number of lattices compatible with these data equals the number
of isometries between the classes of the two Gram matrices, each shifted by a corner term.
The local lattice count of lem-local-lattice-counts-isometries, integrality of the
generators and an integral isomorphism between the two models of the hermitian space
reduce the count to the number of isometries.
Stated with no other statement

Let D be a datum, and suppose the three inputs of lem-local-decomposition-inputs hold
for D. Fix local models at the finite places, types u, u' with T_u ≡ T_(u') mod g^2, a flag,
representative lattices, uniformisers varpi_p and a normalising constant n_c satisfying the
counting formula. Then all local densities are non-negative, and the coefficient of the pair
(u,u') decomposes as a sum over terms γ: each term receives a local class at every place,
compatible with the unramified data off a finite set, and a density. …
Stable approximation gives a representative of each term at every tuple of places. The fibre
counts are functorial and orbits of the zero terms are controlled, so the fibres decompose.
Representatives of the norms exist and move correctly between u and u'. …

Let D be a datum at a point of a family, u ≠ u' two of its types, d_u the dimension of the
representation attached to u, D^ the normalising mass of D (a volume times an index times local
formal degrees), and b its size parameter. Write K_0(u,u') for the off-diagonal term of the
pairing between u and u'. Let a class of families come with a choice of data whose local
components are isomorphic to the standard ones, which satisfies the rank conditions and the
small-terms bound of prop-small-terms-offdiag-level. …
The core is an abstract bound on a pairing over a CM field. Split K_0(u,u') into large,
non-scalar, non-generic and remaining terms. If the first three are small, the local model, the
energy identity and the densities bound the rest by (1+b^(-6)) d_u d_(u')/D^ …

auxiliary fields. Here a datum D at a point of a family carries types u, each with a
finite-dimensional representation of dimension d_u, an integer T_u, a normalising mass D^, a
size parameter b, and for u ≠ u' an off-diagonal term K_0(u, u') (thm-offdiagonal-bound
). Small terms. In the expansion of K_0(u,u'), the large terms and the non-scalar terms each
contribute at most varepsilon_D d_u d_(u')/D^.
The Siegel–Weil formula thm-siegel-main-theorem-hermitian gives the ratio of volumes
of unitary groups under the change M → M-1 of rank. From it follow the rank conditions and
the level bound (3) on the class. …

Suppose that conjugate self-dual and polarized cuspidal representations of GL_a over CM fields
have Galois representations as in thm-galois-reps-csd-above-l and
thm-galois-reps-polarized-cuspidal. Then there is a class of families of definite unitary
groups (def-family) that satisfies the family hypotheses (def-family-data).
Fix the system of local parameters of thm-local-parameters-exist. We build the families
from it, check twelve basic conditions, and derive the family hypotheses from them, in seven
steps.
Members. Siegel's mass formula for standard hermitian lattices over CM fields, as an explicit
ratio involving L(M, η^M), gives the members of the families and admissible data for them (
thm-family-membership-admissible-data). …
Local estimates. Integral models of unitary Shimura varieties bound the depth of the local data
at every prime, explicit exponents bound the index at the twisting places, and the
archimedean weights are bounded below (thm-twisting-index-and-archimedean-bounds
Basic conditions. The families satisfy twelve basic conditions at every admissible datum (
thm-basic-conditions-from-local-parameters).

theorem UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter_of_row (h :
UpperTheory.GalStar.Row0b fun h rc =>
UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.IsRecT h rc) : UpperTheory.EveryCharacter
If polarized pairs have Galois representations (def-galois-reps-polarized), then Dirichlet L
-functions do not vanish right of the critical line (def-nonvanishing-half-plane).
Assume that polarized pairs have Galois representations. The proof walks down the chain of
sec-outline-chain.
From these Galois representations, thm-sha-bound (chap-sha) gives the Tate–Shafarevich
bound with exponent 401 for every primitive character, and thm-local-parameters-exist
gives a system of local parameters. These are the hypotheses of thm-grh-from-sha-bound.
By the theorem of Gelfand and Kazhdan, the Galois representations of polarized pairs give
Galois representations for the cuspidal representations that the families use (
sec-gal-cuspidal). This reduces the claim to thm-grh-from-theta-integrals.
With these, thm-family-data-exists (chap-families) gives a class of families of definite
unitary groups satisfying the family hypotheses. Its inputs come from chap-theta,
chap-heights and chap-sha. This reduces the claim to thm-zero-free-from-families.
… and 1 more paragraphs in the blueprint's proof.

theorem LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re :
DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf
Dirichlet L-functions do not vanish right of the critical line (def-nonvanishing-half-plane).
The proof has two halves, which architecture describes.
The first half is arithmetic. To a polarized regular algebraic cuspidal representation of GL_a
over a CM field we attach a compatible Galois representation (thm-galois-reps-polarized
). We build these from theta lifts between definite unitary groups.
The second half derives the theorem from those Galois representations (
thm-grh-from-galois). They bound Tate–Shafarevich groups along a 2-power cyclotomic
tower. …

theorem riemannHypothesis : RiemannHypothesis
The Riemann Hypothesis (def-riemann-hypothesis) holds.
Let ζ(s) = 0, with s neither a trivial zero nor 1. If Re s > 1/2, this contradicts
lem-zeta-nonvanishing. Suppose Re s < 1/2. Then s ≠ 0, since ζ(0) = -1/2. The
functional equation ζ(1-s) = 2(2π)^(-s) Γ(s)cos(π s/2) ζ(s) holds with s and 1-s
exchanged. …
